A website form talks to n8n through one Webhook node: the browser POSTs the form as JSON, the workflow runs.

Most common mistake: pasting the test URL on the live site. Use the production URL and activate the workflow.

Honeypot trick: add a hidden 'website' field to the form. Humans never see it; many simple bots fill every field. If it's filled, reject the submission in n8n before spending an AI call.

Not perfect, but it stops a lot of junk.

The fastest way to lose a client's trust: the AI invents a price.

Give it a BUSINESS INFO block and one rule: use only those facts, never promise prices or availability that aren't listed, and hand off when unsure. Then review the first 20 replies anyway.

Two habits that stop AI workflows from breaking:
1. Ask for JSON with fixed keys (category, urgent, summary, reply)
2. Parse inside try/catch and fall back to a polite default reply

The patient always hears back, even when the model misbehaves.

Clinic enquiries often include health details, and under UK GDPR health data is 'special category' data.

Basics: a clear privacy notice, limited sheet access, a carefully chosen AI provider, and deleting what you don't need. Not legal advice; the clinic should confirm its own obligations.
